about: How each kind of element is prompted, one recipe per view. `sc.py element add` scaffolds one card per view from these: the layers below are written into the card, and {anchor} is replaced by the element's consistency anchor (one fixed sentence that describes it). Sheets (turnaround, expressions, outfit, product, angles) are shot on a plain background in flat even light, so the model learns the thing and not a place; plates and style frames are shot in the job's own light and look. hf_category is the Higgsfield Elements category the locked element is saved under. A view's finish (clean for sheets) overrides the job's look, so sheets stay neutral; plates, portraits and the style frame keep the job's finish.

character.label: Character (a person, a creature, a mascot)

turnaround.label: Turnaround sheet
turnaround.why: The identity reference: the same body, face, hair and outfit from every side. Video models hold a character best from a clean full-body sheet.

subject.subject: character turnaround sheet of {anchor}: four full-body views side by side, front, three-quarter, profile and back, same neutral standing pose, arms relaxed
subject.consistency: the same one in every panel

world.environment: plain seamless light grey studio background, nothing else in frame

camera.shot_size: full body, head to feet in every view
camera.composition: four evenly spaced views on one row, equal height, nothing cropped

expressions.label: Expression sheet
expressions.why: The faces the script needs, so close-ups keep the same face while acting.

subject.subject: expression sheet of {anchor}: six head-and-shoulders portraits in a two-by-three grid, the same face showing the expressions the script needs, described physically (brows, eyes, mouth)
subject.consistency: the same one in every panel

camera.shot_size: head and shoulders in each panel
camera.composition: even grid, same scale in every panel

outfit.label: Outfit (wardrobe W1, W2...)
outfit.why: One look per outfit change, so wardrobe stays the same across scenes. Add one view per outfit.

subject.subject: full-body front view of {anchor} wearing the outfit, every garment with its colour, material and fit, standing straight

camera.composition: centred, small margin around the figure

portrait.label: Hero portrait in the look
portrait.why: The character in the job's own light and grade: checks the identity holds outside the studio.

subject.subject: {anchor}, natural relaxed pose, looking just off camera

world.environment: a simple setting from the film's world, softly out of focus

light_look.setup: the job's key light (copy from look.md)

environment.label: Environment (a place, a set, a location)

plate.label: Empty establishing plate
plate.why: The place with nobody in it, in the scene's own light and time of day: the background every shot of the scene is built on.

subject.subject: nobody in frame, the set empty and ready for the action

camera.composition: the main playing area in the middle third, clear floor space where people will stand

light_look.setup: the scene's light plan (copy from the environment sheet)

reverse.label: Reverse angle
reverse.why: The opposite side of the same place, so a conversation or a turn has a matching background.

subject.subject: nobody in frame, the same set seen from the opposite direction

light_look.setup: the same light as the plate, seen from the other side

detail.label: Surface and dressing details
detail.why: Close views of the textures and set dressing that close-ups will show.

subject.subject: detail sheet of the set's key surfaces and dressing, four close-up panels, the same place in every panel

time_variant.label: Same place, other time or weather
time_variant.why: When a place appears at two times of day or in different weather. One view per variant.

subject.subject: nobody in frame, the same set from the plate's camera position at another time or weather

prop.label: Prop (an object, a product, a vehicle)

product.label: Clean product shot
product.why: The object alone, sharp and true to colour: shape, material, markings.

subject.subject: {anchor}, alone, in its exact shape, material and colour

camera.shot_size: the whole object filling most of the frame

light_look.setup: soft studio light from above and both sides

angles.label: Multi-angle sheet
angles.why: Front, side, back and top, for props seen from many sides or handled on screen.

subject.subject: multi-angle sheet of {anchor}: front, side, back and top views on one row, same scale
subject.consistency: the same one in every panel

camera.composition: four evenly spaced views, nothing cropped

in_hand.label: Scale in hand
in_hand.why: Shows its size against a hand, so it is never drawn too big or too small.

subject.subject: {anchor} held naturally in one hand, showing its true size

camera.shot_size: close-up on the hand and object

style.label: Style frame (the look: palette, grade, texture)

frame.label: Style frame
frame.why: One representative frame of the finished film: palette, contrast, grain, lens character. Sent as the style reference.

subject.subject: a representative frame of the film: {anchor}
